messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: gradual rollout v3.9.4 shows p95 regressions (+30%) on route 'generation-eu' starting at change-window start. Autorevert scheduled in 2m unless an operator intervenes. telemetry: https://telemetry/redwood/v3.9.4
marco: I see it. This is right after the new batching heuristic landed. Can we hold auto while we try a targeted route pin?
jess: Oncall. Prefer minimal blast radius 539. If it's just generation-eu slices, pin that route in canary back to v3.9.3 instead of full revert.
patrick: Agreed. I'll prepare a short customer blurb in case we widen to full rollback. Also tagging legal for the change-window note. @legal
ops-bot: Autorevert countdown: 120s. Operator override required to suppress.
marco: Proposed steps: 1) suppress autorevert 2) run `rls route-pin --env canary --route generation-eu --to v3.9.3 --reason "p95 regression after batching heuristic"` 3) drain v3.9.4 pods for that route 4) monitor p95 and errors for 20m 5) open a follow-up RL ticket. Who can execute route-pin?
jess: I can run it. Running now: ```bash
rls route-pin --env canary --route generation-eu --to v3.9.3 --reason "p95 regression change-window"
```
ops-bot: Operator override request from jess accepted. Suppressing autorevert for 25m.
ops-bot: Executing: rls route-pin --env canary --route generation-eu --to v3.9.3
ops-bot: SUCCESS: route generation-eu pinned to v3.9.3. Traffic rebalanced accordingly.
marco: After the pin, p95 dropped back close to baseline. Looks like the heuristic increases batching under certain seq-length distributions. I see kvcache churn during the spike.
jess: Leaving pin in place for 30m and collecting traces. I'll also tag the batching change in the PR and add a revert candidate.
pc-bot: (automated) Notifying #customer-updates: "We routed a small portion of traffic to a previous version due to increased latency during a canary rollout. We're investigating and will update within 30 minutes."
patrick: Draft customer-facing line for release notes: "We rolled canary back to v3.9.3 for a subset of Europe traffic due to a performance regression from a new batching heuristic. No customer data was impacted; we're rolling a fix and will resume rollout after validation." Want legal to review before wide customer email?
ops-bot: Note: autorevert suppression will expire at +25m unless extended.
marco: Filing RL-7019 and assigning to runtime + infra with traces and the batching PR diff.
jess: Manual intervention complete: targeted route pin applied, autorevert suppressed, CS update posted, follow-up ticket filed. Will reconvene if noise returns. :white_check_mark:
